en.html:
The fight with the magistrate had taken the <ruby>caloric energy<rt>calories</rt></ruby> in my body nearly to its limit. For this kind of exhaustion there is normally no remedy except food and rest. Easily digested food must go in, and sleep of six hours or more must follow. That is the procedure.

Presently, however, speed ranked above condition. To give the magistrate time was to let him turn the situation around. He had taken a blow and, most probably, was still short of a clear picture of events. This was the moment to chase him. Wait, and the advantage of time would be lost.

So, at a general shop in an inner corner of the village, I selected two or three preserved items and put them into my stomach. A little light movement for digestion. Then defecation, then a short rest.

Two hours, all told.

As replenishment it was only slightly better than doing nothing, but I had refused the trouble of a proper meal, so no complaint is allowed. For a short fight it should hold.

ja.html:
代官との一戦は、体内の<ruby>熱量<rt>カロリー</rt></ruby>をほぼ限度まで奪って
いた。通常、この消耗を補うには食事と休息のほかに
方法がない。消化の良いものを摂取し、六時間以上の
睡眠を取る必要があった。

　しかし現状、迅速な行動は体調の確保に優先する。
代官に時間を与え、巻き返しを許すべきではなかった。
彼が打撃を受け、おそらくは状況把握もまだ不十分で
あろう今の間に追撃せねば、時の利を失う。

　村の奥まった一角で見つけた雑貨屋で、保存食料の
類を二、三みつくろって腹へ収め、軽く体を動かして
消化を促し、脱糞した後少し休む。
　都合二時間。

　何もしないよりはましという程度の補給にしかなら
なかったが、まともな食事を得る手間を惜しんだのだ
から仕方がない。
　この程度でも短時間の戦闘には耐える筈だ。

en.html:
The road was not what one could call fully paved. It had been paved more as a suggestion. No villagers were visible. Perhaps the fields lay in another direction; perhaps they were shut indoors, wary after the disturbance; perhaps it was only the approaching dusk. The sun, I saw, was already in the western sky.

I wanted to finish before night. Whether that would happen was doubtful. It might be difficult.

The season was deep autumn, when sunset is said to fall as quick as a bucket dropped down a well.

en.html:
Her sullen <ruby>metal-echo<rt>metal echo</rt></ruby> arrived directly inside my ears as I threaded through the sea of trees. We could not yet be very deep, but already I could tell neither the way we had come nor the way we were going. Tree, and then tree.

Under morning sun it might have been a pleasant walk. At this hour, with darkness about to fall, any onlooker would see either a test of courage or a wish to die.

More the latter. Every tree had a branch well shaped for hanging something.

　まだそれほど奥深くではない筈だが、既に来た方向
も進行方向も見分けはつかなかった。木、また木。

　朝日の下であれば、気持ちの良い散策になったかも
しれない。
　だがそろそろ暗くなろうかというこの時刻、きっと
傍目には肝試しか自殺志願としか映らないことだろう。

　しかもどちらかといえば後者だ。
　どの木も何かを吊るすには良さそうな枝ぶりである。

en.html:
...The bad prediction came true. It usually does.

There was a person. A medium-height figure in a school uniform, back toward us. A village youth, perhaps? He was <ruby>crouched<rt>crouched</rt></ruby>, hugging his own legs, in front of <ruby>something<rt>・・</rt></ruby>.

Something. For an ordinary animal, this angle would have hidden it behind the human figure. But <ruby>what<rt>・・</rt></ruby> it was, was clear at one glance. Which meant it was not ordinary.

A dog. A mountain dog, probably. The evil glint in the eyes and the ragged coat set it a thick line apart from dogs seen among people. It looked like one of those dangerous roamers of mountain and field, these days often called "the Honorable Government" as a jab at Rokuhara.

But the body was abnormal. It seemed nearly the size of a small bear. Standing on its hind legs, would it not reach almost human height? Even speaking modestly, no ordinary dog.

But the body was abnormal. It seemed nearly the size of a small bear. Standing on its hind legs, would it not reach almost human height? Even speaking modestly, no ordinary dog.

en.html: A beast of that degree could be killed bare-handed. But that was not what my answer meant. I slowed my run, muffled my steps, and crept closer. A noisy intrusion might startle the figure and give the beast its chance. To push unneeded・・・・・ help on someone and then produce that result would be too pathetic. At a suitable distance I stopped and hid behind a convenient tree. The mountain dog, however, had probably noticed the newcomer. Perhaps judging that the situation had moved, it gave one shrill bark like a final ultimatum.◆¦ Before the echo died, it bared its fangs and sprang at the figure, still motionless to the point of indifference. Fast. A straight, angular charge, peculiar to dogs, not like a cat's. Unless you had kept well away, nobody standing this close could meet that charge head-on and still dodge. The figure, at last, was getting up. The slow lifting of his head was more bear-like than the attacking monster-dog. Much duller. Much slower. The dog ran. The figure stood. Contact. In that instant, the one who achieved his intention was not the dog-monster that had raced several ken for the throat of its target.
en.text:
A beast of that degree could be killed bare-handed. But that was not what my answer meant.

I slowed my run, muffled my steps, and crept closer. A noisy intrusion might startle the figure and give the beast its chance.

To push unneeded・・・・・ help on someone and then produce that result would be too pathetic. At a suitable distance I stopped and hid behind a convenient tree.

The mountain dog, however, had probably noticed the newcomer. Perhaps judging that the situation had moved, it gave one shrill bark like a final ultimatum.◆¦ Before the echo died, it bared its fangs and sprang at the figure, still motionless to the point of indifference.

Fast. A straight, angular charge, peculiar to dogs, not like a cat's. Unless you had kept well away, nobody standing this close could meet that charge head-on and still dodge.

The figure, at last, was getting up.

The slow lifting of his head was more bear-like than the attacking monster-dog. Much duller. Much slower.

The dog ran. The figure stood.

Contact.

In that instant, the one who achieved his intention was not the dog-monster that had raced several ken for the throat of its target.

ja.html: あの程度の獣ならば生身で駆逐できるだろう。 　もっとも、そういう意味での返答ではなかった。 　走る速度を緩める。足音を殺し、忍び寄った。 　けたたましい乱入は人影を驚かせ、獣の側に好機を 与える結果となりかねない。 　要りもせぬ・・・・・助けを押し付けた挙句にそれでは、余り に情けないというものだった。 　ある程度の距離まで接近したところで足を止めて、 手頃な木の陰に身を隠す。 　しかし、山犬は新手の到来に気付いたのだろう。 　状況が動いたとを察しての判断か、最後通牒のよう に甲高く吠える――◆¦ そしてその残響の絶えぬ内、尚も 無関心なまでに不動の姿へ、牙を剥くや噛み掛かった。 　迅い。 　猫科の獣とはまた異なる、犬類特有の直線的、鋭角 的な突進。よほどに距離を置いていたならばともかく、 指呼の間合でこれを迎えて躱せるものではあるまい。 　人影は、漸ようよう、起き上がっていた。 　のっそりと首をもたげるその動きは、襲い来る山犬 の怪物よりもむしろ熊じみている。 　格段に鈍く、遅い。 　犬が駆ける。 　人影が起つ。 　 　――接触する。 　その一刹那。 　企図を遂げていたのは、数間を疾駆して標的の首筋 を狙った犬怪ではなかった。
ja.text:
あの程度の獣ならば生身で駆逐できるだろう。
　もっとも、そういう意味での返答ではなかった。

　走る速度を緩める。足音を殺し、忍び寄った。
　けたたましい乱入は人影を驚かせ、獣の側に好機を
与える結果となりかねない。

　要りもせぬ・・・・・助けを押し付けた挙句にそれでは、余り
に情けないというものだった。
　ある程度の距離まで接近したところで足を止めて、
手頃な木の陰に身を隠す。

　しかし、山犬は新手の到来に気付いたのだろう。
　状況が動いたとを察しての判断か、最後通牒のよう
に甲高く吠える――◆¦

そしてその残響の絶えぬ内、尚も
無関心なまでに不動の姿へ、牙を剥くや噛み掛かった。

　迅い。
　猫科の獣とはまた異なる、犬類特有の直線的、鋭角
的な突進。よほどに距離を置いていたならばともかく、
指呼の間合でこれを迎えて躱せるものではあるまい。

　人影は、漸ようよう、起き上がっていた。

　のっそりと首をもたげるその動きは、襲い来る山犬
の怪物よりもむしろ熊じみている。
　格段に鈍く、遅い。

　犬が駆ける。
　人影が起つ。
　
　――接触する。

　その一刹那。
　企図を遂げていたのは、数間を疾駆して標的の首筋
を狙った犬怪ではなかった。

en.html:
The first contact was between the figure's right fist and the charging mountain dog.
It was <ruby>the dog's own force<rt>・・・・・</rt></ruby> that made the impact decisive.

The figure had used no more strength than was needed to <ruby>place his fist there<rt>・・・・・・・</rt></ruby>.

The animal cried out, was thrown back through the air, and fell near where it had begun. For a moment I could only watch.

The student finished rising and walked over.
The dog was dying.

Its own tremendous strength had brought this about. At least it had not suffered long. An irony, and a pitiable one.

Had the student hesitated over whether to finish it? His approaching step faltered.
While he paused, it was over.

The last breath ceased. Silence returned to the forest, and a lingering unease showed in the figure's back.

Looking at that back, I—

時間軸上、最も早く重なった両者の部位は、人影の
右拳と山犬の咽喉だった。
　拳の先端が、脆弱な骨格に突き刺さる――刺される
<ruby>犬自身の力<rt>・・・・・</rt></ruby>がそうさせる。

　針山へ蜜柑を投げ込むようなもの。
　人影は、ただ、<ruby>そこへ拳を置く<rt>・・・・・・・</rt></ruby>以上の力を使っては
いない。

　くきゃり……という短くも滑稽な音を聞いたように
思った。
　あるいは錯覚だったろうか。


　その直後の悲痛な絶叫と、まるで曲芸を仕込まれて
いるかのように宙へ舞い、弧を描きつつ元の位置まで
転げ落ちていく大柄な山犬の姿は、一瞬、忘我を避け
得ないほど印象的なものであったから。


　落ちた犬が、のたうつ――激しく、短く。
　学生服の人物が完全に立ち上がり、犬の傍まで歩み
寄った頃には、既にその四肢の痙攣は弱いものとなり、
か細く末期の息を洩らすばかりになっていた。

　一撃は喉ばかりでなく、頚骨まで砕いたのだろう。
　犬の怪力がその結果を導いた。お陰で長く苦しまず
に済んだ――そう思えば皮肉であり、哀れであった。

　止めを与えるべきか、その人は迷ったのだろうか。
近付く足がふと、たたらを踏む。
　その間に、終わっていた。最後の呼吸が絶え、森に
静寂が戻る。そして人影の背には後味の悪さが滲んだ。

　その背を見て、俺は――
